subject.title: Model fallback can deliver a duplicate reply when a fully-delivered primary attempt is re-classified as a failure

question: For fallback after a thrown model attempt, should OpenClaw suppress retry only after completed terminal delivery, or after any committed outbound side effect?
rationale: The existing delivery helpers encode different valid semantics: one protects user-turn completion and the other protects recovery after any external side effect. Choosing between them changes whether an interim status message may recover through a fallback model.

options.title: Use terminal-delivery semantics
options.body: Allow fallback after progress-only output, but stop it once the source turn has a completed final reply; this is recommended because it prevents duplicate answers without sacrificing recovery after interim status.

options.title: Use any-side-effect semantics
options.body: Stop fallback after any committed outbound action, prioritizing avoidance of repeated external effects at the cost of leaving progress-only failed turns unrecovered.

options.title: Specify a new explicit fallback-delivery contract
options.body: Define a dedicated turn-scoped signal if neither existing predicate exactly captures the intended retry boundary.

recommendation.title: Use terminal-delivery semantics
recommendation.body: Allow fallback after progress-only output, but stop it once the source turn has a completed final reply; this is recommended because it prevents duplicate answers without sacrificing recovery after interim status.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related issue already owns the broader durable final-delivery contract that this fallback decision depends on.
